column1: A WSI of colorectal cancer with low-grade tumor budding at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a relatively sharply defined and cohesive invasive front, smooth or pushing tumor margins, and an absence or extreme rarity of detached small cellular islands in the adjacent peritumoral stroma.

A WSI of colorectal cancer with intermediate-grade tumor budding at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of an irregular or jagged invasive margin, characterized by a moderate dispersion of small, disconnected cellular aggregates breaking away from the main tumor mass into the adjacent reactive stroma.

A WSI of colorectal cancer with high-grade tumor budding at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a highly infiltrative, hazy, and ill-defined invasive front, widespread dissociation of the tumor mass, and numerous fine cellular aggregates extensively dispersed deep into the prominent desmoplastic stroma.

A WSI of colorectal cancer with low-grade tumor budding at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of continuous malignant epithelial structures, with 0 to 4 detached single tumor cells or small clusters (comprising fewer than 5 cells) visible within the desmoplastic stroma at the advancing edge of the tumor.

A WSI of colorectal cancer with intermediate-grade tumor budding at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of partial loss of epithelial cohesion, with 5 to 9 detached single tumor cells or small clusters (comprising fewer than 5 cells) scattered within the dense peritumoral stroma at the invasive front.

A WSI of colorectal cancer with high-grade tumor budding at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe loss of cellular cohesion, featuring 10 or more detached single tumor cells or small clusters (comprising fewer than 5 cells) densely infiltrating the peritumoral stroma, frequently accompanied by an active fibrotic reaction.
